hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Paisalo Digital as a 34-year-old, AA/Stable-rated NBFC "bridging India's credit gap" — an asset-light, partnership-led lender delivering last-mile MSME and micro-enterprise credit to unbanked and underserved borrowers through 5,995 touch points, with AI embedded across the lending lifecycle.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Bridging the credit gap": formal credit for unbanked and underserved borrowers, including MSMEs, with tailored loan offerings designed around varied borrower needs and local cash flows.
- 34 years of legacy (incorporated 1992, listed 1996), dual credit rating of AA/Stable/A1+ (AA Stable assigned by Infomerics Ratings and AA Stable by Brickwork Ratings), and a customer franchise of 18 mn+.
- Partnership-led model on two fronts: 5 co-lending partners that "extend access and balance-sheet depth", and Business Correspondent partnerships with State Bank of India, Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank for last-mile BaaS delivery.
- Three-year vision rests on three planks: an AI-led lending franchise, best-in-class asset quality targeted at sub-2% through the cycles, and scale ambition of ~2x growth in AUM, Income and PAT over the next three years at a CAGR of ~25-30%.
- Portfolio is geographically concentrated: state-wise breakup shows Delhi 27.1%, Maharashtra 19.4%, Uttar Pradesh 14.9%, Haryana 13.0%, Rajasthan 12.6%, Others 13%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Promoters continue to purchase shares from the open market, raising stake to 46.7% (+4.97% during Q1FY27), which the deck reads as "signaling strong long-term commitment in the growth journey".
- Liability diversification is a stated structural lever: approved and launched Tranche I public issue of secured, rated, listed NCDs aggregating up to Rs 300 Cr under a Rs 900 Cr shelf limit in August 2026 (opening date 7th Aug'26), alongside a maiden ECB issuance of USD 15 Mn and a first FCCB issue of USD 50 Mn.
- Borrowing mix at Q1FY27 as presented: Banks and FIs 73%, FCCBs 17%, NCDs 8%, Commercial Paper 2% — versus Banks and FIs 77% / NCDs 23% at FY23.
- Capital adequacy of 33.1% (Tier I 26.8%, Tier II 6.3%) is described as "comfortably above the 15% regulatory minimum — a strong buffer to fund growth", with Debt/Equity at 2.61x rising from 1.64x at FY22 as the balance sheet is levered up.
- Co-lending economics are structurally capital-light: 80:20 participation with the bank contributing 80%, only 20% of the loan recognised on Paisalo's balance sheet, credit costs shared pari-passu 80:20 with no FLDG, and earnings from spread on the 20% portion plus processing and partner fee income.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [ALM] The deck reports a consistently positive ALM gap across all buckets — assets vs liabilities of 17,025 vs 8,550 (<6 Months), 13,361 vs 6,223 (<1 Year) and 26,521 vs 21,781 (<3 Year) in Rs Mn — which it says strengthens liquidity and reduces refinancing risk; liquidity coverage is cited at 2.3x.
- [Capital structure] Outstanding GDRs were successfully converted in Q2FY26; the deck notes FY15-FY23 share data is adjusted for a 1:10 stock split in June 2022 and a 1:1 bonus issue in March 2024.
- [Underwriting model] Because the target market lacks bureau history and formal income proof (no ITR), underwriting relies on on-ground verification, cash-flow assessment via store/business visits, proxy indicators (asset ownership, rent, electricity usage, staff employed), geospatial mapping and a "3 Cs — Character, Credit and Credibility" assessment, combined with centralized AI/ML underwriting.
- [Collections] In-house debt management infrastructure with a three-stage escalation (Normal / Initial delinquency / NPA), sales incentives linked to collection performance, and 91% of collections done digitally in Q1FY27.
- [Shareholding] Annexure lists market capitalization of Rs 54.1 Bn, ~910 Mn outstanding shares, 92K shareholders and dividend of 10%; June-26 shareholding is Promoter and Promoter Group 46.72%, DII 6.83%, FII 6.79%, Others 39.66%, with fully diluted promoter holding of 42.88%.
